rationale: bugs_open/277, owner ruling 2026-08-15: 'we should create a repair handler fleet wide' for required_fields_missing — the type is filed flag-only (HandlerAgent "", needs_human_review) by check_required_fields_missing.go, so every item parks unread; exactly one item in platform history has ever reached a terminal status. This is one type's instance of bugs_open/033's owner-ruled reframing (2026-07-25: 'the framework — not a person — should resolve every one of these classes'). The change follows the estate's established router-not-repairer pattern (IMG-071 / seed 397, owner-instructed 2026-08-12, executed in production): a pure-SQL DB-config agent that classifies each item once by (page_name, slot_name) — the revalidator's own key, never spec.component_id which is unstable across rerenders — and then CONVERTS the two classes that have an owning repair path, CLOSES the two classes whose predicate no longer holds, and PARKS-IN-PLACE (back to needs_human_review, holding the dedup key, with the facts and safe options in the error message) the two classes that must not be auto-repaired: blob components (NULL content_data under 1.5-21KB of serving rendered_html — regeneration would REPLACE served HTML with one template render, bugs_open/263's class) and owned/tool pages with no plan (the owned-page guard, itself an owner ruling, refuses generic rebuild). Park-in-place rather than checkpoint-and-complete is deliberate: checkpoint_for_review writes NO item_key (no dedup) and completing the original releases its dedup key, so the producer re-raises and the two-strike rule births endless unresolved rows (5 keys of this very type already sat at 1 strike on 2026-08-04); a held dedup key makes churn structurally impossible. Census of all 44 open items run 2026-08-15 (read-only, saved with the workstream docs): no_content_data 35, stale 6, no_plan_generic 1, no_plan_owned 1 (the owner's worked example, gaswholesalers tool-gas-unit-converter), partial 1.
